title: Mi piace, mi piacciono
summary: The piacere construction — mi piace vs mi piacciono, the classic beginner trap.

blocks.title: Il trucco di piacere
blocks.body: *Piacere* works backwards from English 'to like': the **thing liked** is the grammatical subject, and the person is an indirect object. So it's **mi piace il caffè** (literally 'coffee is pleasing to me') with one thing, but **mi piacciono i libri** with more than one. Before an infinitive, it's always singular: **mi piace leggere** (I like to read).
blocks.callout: Check the noun after *piace/piacciono*, not 'I' — singular thing → *piace*, plural things → *piacciono*.

blocks.title: Non solo 'mi'
blocks.body: *Piacere* uses the same indirect-object pronouns you'll meet everywhere else.

pairs.left: *mi piace* — one thing or an infinitive: *mi piace il vino*
pairs.right: *mi piacciono* — more than one thing: *mi piacciono i tortellini*
pairs.note: The classic beginner trap: don't conjugate for 'I', conjugate for what's liked.

blocks.prompt: How do you say 'I like the books' (i libri)?
blocks.explain: *I libri* is plural, so the verb has to be *piacciono* — it agrees with the books, not with 'I'.
*Mi piace il caffè.* — one thing, singular *piace*.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

lines.target: Non mi piace il pesce crudo.

blocks.scene: Giulia asks about your food tastes over an aperitivo in Bologna

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: Allora, ti piace la cucina bolognese?
lines.en: So, do you like Bologna cooking?

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Sì, mi piacciono molto i tortellini.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: E la mortadella? A me piace tantissimo.
lines.spotlight: *A me piace* doubles the pronoun for emphasis — the 'mi' is still there, just reinforced.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Mi piace, ma non mi piace il fegato.
lines.en: I like it, but I don't like liver.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: Guarda, neanche a Marco piace il fegato — sei in buona compagnia.
lines.en: Look, Marco doesn't like liver either — you're in good company.

blocks.prompt: Write three sentences about your own food tastes: something you like a lot, something you like less, and one thing using mi piace + an infinitive (e.g., mi piace cucinare).
